paper_title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for Multi-Agent Collaborative Software Development
core_problem: Existing LLM-based multi-agent systems can solve simple dialogue tasks but suffer logic inconsistencies and cascading hallucinations when naively chaining LLMs for complex tasks, leading to incoherent solutions and ineffective replication of human workflows.
methodology_summary: MetaGPT is a meta-programming framework that incorporates efficient human workflows into LLM-based multi-agent collaborations. It encodes Standardized Operating Procedures into prompt sequences for streamlined workflows, uses an assembly line paradigm to assign diverse roles to agents to break down complex tasks into subtasks, enables agents with human-like domain expertise to verify intermediate results and reduce errors, and requires agents to generate structured outputs such as high-quality requirements.
datasets_eval: HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021a) and MBPP (Austin et al., 2021) for code generation evaluation; collaborative software engineering benchmarks.
empirical_results: MetaGPT generates more coherent solutions than previous chat-based multi-agent systems on collaborative software engineering benchmarks. On code generation benchmarks it achieves a new state-of-the-art Pass@1 of 85.9% on HumanEval and 87.7% on MBPP, outperforming frameworks such as AutoGPT, LangChain and AgentVerse for complex software project creation.
explicit_limitations: No explicit limitations are detailed in the provided context; the text notes that autonomous agents using LLMs offer promising opportunities but existing systems tend to oversimplify complexities and struggle to achieve effective, coherent performance in real-world applications.
